svg.font-family: Outfit, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: wherry credential delivery
svg.desc: Sequence of one seal across the host, the tenant feed, the host topic, the receiver, its plugin and the job. The receiver makes a P-256 key pair for the attempt, starts reading the host topic from its end, and writes a signed seal request to the tenant feed naming the run, attempt, public key, credential names and an expiry 5 minutes out. The host's wherry await or wherry mcp reads it, checks it under a lock on the attempt, resolves each credential from its file, environment or command source, presigns any S3 URLs and adds the run's redaction key, then writes an unsigned seal, a compact JWE to the request's key whose header binds the run and attempt, to its host topic. The receiver opens it with the attempt's private key, checks the binding, expiry and URLs, and passes the values to the plugin in Dispatch, which delivers each credential to its target, an environment variable or a file in the credentials directory, and fetches S3 inputs without exposing their URLs to the job. Everything the receiver publishes for the attempt carries markers in place of the values. With no seal in 5 minutes the run fails with a message naming the credentials. Credential values in the clear, the storage credential, the host's signing key and its bundle stay on the host; the attempt's private key stays in the receiver's memory.
